summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Sheikh Zayed Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as Sri Lanka posted 419/10 (154.6 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Pakistan countered with 422/10 (162.3 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 6-Wicket Spell: HMRKB Herath (6/43), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, HMRKB Herath delivered a masterclass for Sri Lanka (4 Runs & 11 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Sri Lanka 52%) and allowing Sri Lanka to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Pakistan faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Sri Lanka's bowling unit, bolstered by Yasir Shah (14 Runs & 9 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Sri Lanka won by 21 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Sri Lanka's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Pakistan produced fighting phases, Sri Lanka won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
